4	date : "2026-06-01"

7	
8	#### The Congruence Lattice of a Setoid Algebra
9	
10	This is the [Setoid.Congruences.Lattice][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
11	
12	The congruences of an algebra `𝑨`, ordered by containment, form a complete lattice.
13	This module begins the formalization of that fact by promoting `Con 𝑨` to a
14	first-class ordered object: it defines the containment order `_⊆_`, the induced
15	equivalence `_≑_` of mutual containment, and the **meet** `θ ∧ φ`, which is the
16	relational intersection `θ ∩ φ`.  The intersection of two congruences is again a
17	congruence, and it is the greatest lower bound of the two arguments.  Thus we have a
18	partially ordered set which, with the meet operation, forms a semilattice.
19	
20	<!--
21	```agda
22	{-# OPTIONS --cubical-compatible --exact-split --safe #-}
23	
24	module Setoid.Congruences.Lattice where
25	
26	-- Imports from the Agda Standard Library ---------------------------------------
27	open import Agda.Primitive           using () renaming ( Set to Type )
28	open import Data.Product             using ( _×_ ; _,_ ; proj₁ ; proj₂ ; swap )
29	open import Data.Unit.Base           using ( tt )
30	open import Level                    using ( Level ; _⊔_ ; lift ; lower )
31	open import Relation.Binary          using ( Setoid ; IsEquivalence ; IsPartialOrder ; _⇒_ )
32	                                     renaming ( Rel to BinaryRel )
33	open import Relation.Binary.Bundles  using ( Poset )
34	open import Relation.Binary.Lattice  using ( Infimum ; IsMeetSemilattice ; MeetSemilattice )
35	
36	-- Imports from the Agda Universal Algebras Library ------------------------------
37	open import Overture                  using  ( 𝑆 )
38	open import Setoid.Algebras.Basic     using  ( ov ; Algebra ; 𝕌[_] ; 𝔻[_] )
39	open import Setoid.Congruences.Basic  using  ( Con ; mkcon ; _∣≈_ ; reflexive
40	                                             ; is-equivalence ; is-compatible
41	                                             ; 𝟘[_] ; 𝟙[_] )
42	private variable α ρ ℓ : Level
43	```
44	-->
45	
46	#### The containment order on congruences
47	
48	For congruences `θ φ : Con 𝑨` we write `θ ⊆ φ` when the underlying relation of `θ`
49	is **contained** in that of `φ` ("contained" is with respect to subset inclusion on
50	`ℙ(A × A)`).  Classically this is the familiar (lattice) partial order on equivalence
51	relations, and it remains a partial order here — `_⊆_` is antisymmetric
52	**with respect to `_≑_`**, the equivalence of *mutual set containment*.  The only
53	subtlety is which equality counts as **equal congruences**.
54	
55	The underlying relation of a congruence inhabits the `BinaryRel` type
56	(`BinaryRel A ℓ = A → A → Type ℓ`), so mutual containment yields back-and-forth maps
57	between the proof-types `proj₁ θ x y` and `proj₁ φ x y` rather than a proof that the
58	packaged congruences are *propositionally* equal.
59	
60	Upgrading `_≑_` to propositional equality would need function extensionality with
61	propositional extensionality/univalence (and proof-irrelevance for the `IsCongruence`
62	witness), and that's simply not available under   `--safe --cubical-compatible`; so we
63	take `_≑_` as the equality of congruences, exactly as the `Setoid/` discipline
64	dictates.  Classically `_≑_` collapses to propositional equality via propositional
65	extensionality.
66	
67	```agda
68	module _ {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ} where
69	  -- θ ⊆ φ : the relation of θ is contained in the relation of φ.
70	  _⊆_ : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
71	  θ ⊆ φ = proj₁ θ ⇒ proj₁ φ
72	  infix 4 _⊆_
73	
74	  -- θ ≑ φ : mutual containment (the equivalence the partial order is taken over).
75	  -- (the symbol ≑ is input as \doteqdot)
76	  _≑_ : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
77	  θ ≑ φ = θ ⊆ φ × φ ⊆ θ
78	  infix 4 _≑_
79	
80	  -- TODO: consider defining _≑_ as follows instead:
81	  -- _≑_ : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
82	  -- θ ≑ φ = θ .proj₁ ≐ φ .proj₁
83	  -- where ≐ is mutual containment of predicates defined in Relation.Unary.
84	```
85	
86	The order is reflexive and transitive, and `_≑_` collapses it to a partial order.
87	
88	```agda
89	  ⊆-refl : {θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ⊆ θ
90	  ⊆-refl p = p
91	
92	  ⊆-trans : {θ φ ψ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ⊆ φ → φ ⊆ ψ → θ ⊆ ψ
93	  ⊆-trans θ⊆φ φ⊆ψ p = φ⊆ψ (θ⊆φ p)
94	
95	  -- A ≑-step entails a ⊆-step (the `reflexive` field of a preorder).
96	  ⊆-reflexive : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ≑ φ → θ ⊆ φ
97	  ⊆-reflexive = proj₁
98	
99	  -- Antisymmetry holds up to mutual containment, by definition of _≑_.
100	  ⊆-antisym : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ⊆ φ → φ ⊆ θ → θ ≑ φ
101	  ⊆-antisym θ⊆φ φ⊆θ = θ⊆φ , φ⊆θ
102	
103	  -- The components are written out directly rather than via ⊆-refl/⊆-trans:
104	  -- because _⊆_ is a defined relation (not an injective type former), Agda
105	  -- cannot recover the implicit congruence arguments of those lemmas from the
106	  -- expected component types, so we inline the (trivial) proofs here.
107	  ≑-refl : {θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ≑ θ
108	  ≑-refl = (λ z → z) , (λ z → z)
109	
110	  ≑-sym : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ≑ φ → φ ≑ θ
111	  ≑-sym = swap
112	
113	  ≑-trans : {θ φ ψ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ≑ φ → φ ≑ ψ → θ ≑ ψ
114	  ≑-trans (θ⊆φ , φ⊆θ) (φ⊆ψ , ψ⊆φ) = (λ p → φ⊆ψ (θ⊆φ p)) , (λ p → φ⊆θ (ψ⊆φ p))
115	
116	  -- The implicit congruence (and level) arguments of the helper lemmas are bound
117	  -- by lambdas and forwarded explicitly: they cannot be inferred through the
118	  -- (non-injective) `Con 𝑨 ℓ` carrier type at these function-typed fields.
119	  ≑-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence (_≑_ {ℓ})
120	  ≑-isEquivalence {ℓ} = record
121	    { refl = λ {θ} → ≑-refl {ℓ} {θ}
122	    ; sym = λ {θ} {φ} → ≑-sym {ℓ} {θ} {φ}
123	    ; trans = λ {θ} {φ} {ψ} → ≑-trans  {ℓ} {θ} {φ} {ψ}
124	    }
125	
126	  ⊆-isPartialOrder : IsPartialOrder (_≑_ {ℓ}) _⊆_
127	  ⊆-isPartialOrder {ℓ} = record
128	    { isPreorder = record  { isEquivalence = ≑-isEquivalence {ℓ}
129	                           ; reflexive = λ {θ} {φ} → ⊆-reflexive {ℓ} {θ} {φ}
130	                           ; trans = λ {θ} {φ} {ψ} → ⊆-trans {ℓ} {θ} {φ} {ψ}
131	                           }
132	    ; antisym = λ {θ} {φ} → ⊆-antisym {ℓ} {θ} {φ}
133	    }
134	```
135	
136	#### The bottom and top of the order
137	
138	The diagonal congruence `𝟘[ 𝑨 ]` (defined in [Setoid.Congruences.Basic][]) is the
139	*least* congruence: it is contained in every congruence, because a congruence is
140	reflexive over `≈` and `𝟘[ 𝑨 ]` relates only `≈`-equal pairs.  The total congruence
141	`𝟙[ 𝑨 ]` is the *greatest*: every congruence is contained in it, since it relates
142	everything.  These are the `⊥` and `⊤` of the congruence lattice.
143	
144	```agda
145	  -- 𝟘[ 𝑨 ] is the least congruence (the minimum of the containment order).
146	  𝟘-min : {ℓ : Level}(θ : Con 𝑨 (ρ ⊔ ℓ)) → 𝟘[ 𝑨 ] {ℓ} ⊆ θ
147	  𝟘-min θ p = reflexive (proj₂ θ) (lower p)
148	
149	  -- 𝟙[ 𝑨 ] is the greatest congruence (the maximum of the containment order).
150	  𝟙-max : {ℓ : Level}(θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → θ ⊆ 𝟙[ 𝑨 ] {ℓ}
151	  𝟙-max θ _ = lift tt
152	```
153	
154	#### Meet: the intersection of two congruences
155	
156	The intersection `θ ∩ φ` holds at `(x , y)` exactly when both `θ` and `φ` do.  It
157	is again a congruence: it contains the setoid equality (reflexivity), it is an
158	equivalence relation (componentwise), and it is compatible with every basic
159	operation (componentwise, using the compatibility of `θ` and of `φ`).  We define
160	the underlying relation first, then bundle the `IsCongruence` proof.
161	
162	```agda
163	  -- The underlying relation of the meet: pointwise conjunction.
164	  meetRel : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → BinaryRel 𝕌[ 𝑨 ] ℓ
165	  meetRel θ φ x y = proj₁ θ x y × proj₁ φ x y
166	
167	  _∧_ : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ
168	  θ ∧ φ = meetRel θ φ , mkcon m-reflexive m-isEquivalence m-compatible
169	    where
170	    θc = proj₂ θ
171	    φc = proj₂ φ
172	    θe = is-equivalence θc
173	    φe = is-equivalence φc
174	
175	    open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] using ( _≈_ )
176	    -- The meet contains the setoid equality because θ and φ both do.
177	    m-reflexive : ∀ {a₀ a₁} → a₀ ≈ a₁ → meetRel θ φ a₀ a₁
178	    m-reflexive e = reflexive θc e , reflexive φc e
179	
180	    open IsEquivalence using (refl ; sym ; trans )
181	    -- The meet is an equivalence relation, proved componentwise.
182	    m-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence (meetRel θ φ)
183	    m-isEquivalence .refl = θe .refl , φe .refl
184	    m-isEquivalence .sym = λ (p , q) → θe .sym p , φe .sym q
185	    m-isEquivalence .trans = λ (p , q) (p′ , q′) → θe .trans p p′ , φe .trans q q′
186	
187	    -- The meet is compatible with every basic operation, componentwise.
188	    m-compatible : 𝑨 ∣≈ meetRel θ φ
189	    m-compatible 𝑓 uv = is-compatible θc 𝑓 (λ i → proj₁ (uv i))
190	                      , is-compatible φc 𝑓 (λ i → proj₂ (uv i))
191	  infixl 7 _∧_
192	```
193	
194	The meet is the *greatest lower bound* of its two arguments: it is below each of
195	them, and it is above any common lower bound.  These three facts are exactly the
196	`Infimum` of `_⊆_` at `_∧_`.
197	
198	```agda
199	  ∧-lowerˡ : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ∧ φ ⊆ θ
200	  ∧-lowerˡ = proj₁
201	
202	  ∧-lowerʳ : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ∧ φ ⊆ φ
203	  ∧-lowerʳ = proj₂
204	
205	  ∧-greatest : {θ φ ψ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → ψ ⊆ θ → ψ ⊆ φ → ψ ⊆ θ ∧ φ
206	  ∧-greatest ψ⊆θ ψ⊆φ p = ψ⊆θ p , ψ⊆φ p
207	
208	  -- As above, the implicit congruence arguments of ∧-lowerˡ/ʳ and ∧-greatest
209	  -- are not inferable from the expected component types, so we inline them.
210	  ∧-infimum : Infimum (_⊆_ {ℓ}) _∧_
211	  ∧-infimum θ φ = proj₁ , proj₂ , λ ψ ψ⊆θ ψ⊆φ p → ψ⊆θ p , ψ⊆φ p
212	
213	  open IsMeetSemilattice
214	
215	  ∧-isMeetSemilattice : IsMeetSemilattice (_≑_ {ℓ}) _⊆_ _∧_
216	  ∧-isMeetSemilattice .isPartialOrder = ⊆-isPartialOrder
217	  ∧-isMeetSemilattice .infimum = ∧-infimum
218	```
219	
220	#### The poset and meet-semilattice of congruences
221	
222	Finally we assemble the standard-library bundles.  At a fixed relation level `ℓ`,
223	`Con-Poset 𝑨` is the poset `(Con 𝑨, ≑, ⊆)` and `Con-MeetSemilattice 𝑨` equips it
224	with the meet `_∧_`.  (The full lattice and complete lattice, with the join and
225	the bounds `⊥`/`⊤`, are built in the subsequent steps of #271.)
226	
227	```agda
228	module _ (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ) {ℓ : Level} where
229	  Con-Poset : Poset (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ)
230	  Con-Poset = record  { Carrier = Con 𝑨 ℓ ; _≈_ = _≑_ ; _≤_ = _⊆_
231	                      ; isPartialOrder  = ⊆-isPartialOrder }
232	
233	  Con-MeetSemilattice : MeetSemilattice (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ)
234	  Con-MeetSemilattice = record  { Carrier = Con 𝑨 ℓ
235	                                ; _≈_ = _≑_
236	                                ; _≤_ = _⊆_
237	                                ; _∧_ = _∧_
238	                                ; isMeetSemilattice  = ∧-isMeetSemilattice
239	                                }
240	```

#### The containment order on congruences

`ℙ(A × A)`).  Classically this is the familiar (lattice) partial order on equivalence
relations, and it remains a partial order here — `_⊆_` is antisymmetric
**with respect to `_≑_`**, the equivalence of *mutual set containment*.  The only
subtlety is which equality counts as **equal congruences**.

The underlying relation of a congruence inhabits the `BinaryRel` type
(`BinaryRel A ℓ = A → A → Type ℓ`), so mutual containment yields back-and-forth maps
between the proof-types `proj₁ θ x y` and `proj₁ φ x y` rather than a proof that the
packaged congruences are *propositionally* equal.

Upgrading `_≑_` to propositional equality would need function extensionality with
propositional extensionality/univalence (and proof-irrelevance for the `IsCongruence`
witness), and that's simply not available under   `--safe --cubical-compatible`; so we

dictates.  Classically `_≑_` collapses to propositional equality via propositional
extensionality.

```agda
module _ {𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ} where
  -- θ ⊆ φ : the relation of θ is contained in the relation of φ.
  _⊆_ : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
  θ ⊆ φ = proj₁ θ ⇒ proj₁ φ
  infix 4 _⊆_

  -- θ ≑ φ : mutual containment (the equivalence the partial order is taken over).
  -- (the symbol ≑ is input as \doteqdot)
  _≑_ : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
  θ ≑ φ = θ ⊆ φ × φ ⊆ θ
  infix 4 _≑_

  -- TODO: consider defining _≑_ as follows instead:
  -- _≑_ : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
  -- θ ≑ φ = θ .proj₁ ≐ φ .proj₁
  -- where ≐ is mutual containment of predicates defined in Relation.Unary.
```

The order is reflexive and transitive, and `_≑_` collapses it to a partial order.

```agda
  ⊆-refl : {θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ⊆ θ

  ⊆-trans : {θ φ ψ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ⊆ φ → φ ⊆ ψ → θ ⊆ ψ
  ⊆-trans θ⊆φ φ⊆ψ p = φ⊆ψ (θ⊆φ p)

  -- A ≑-step entails a ⊆-step (the `reflexive` field of a preorder).
  ⊆-reflexive : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ≑ φ → θ ⊆ φ
  ⊆-reflexive = proj₁

  -- Antisymmetry holds up to mutual containment, by definition of _≑_.
  ⊆-antisym : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ⊆ φ → φ ⊆ θ → θ ≑ φ
  ⊆-antisym θ⊆φ φ⊆θ = θ⊆φ , φ⊆θ

  -- The components are written out directly rather than via ⊆-refl/⊆-trans:
  -- because _⊆_ is a defined relation (not an injective type former), Agda
  -- cannot recover the implicit congruence arguments of those lemmas from the
  -- expected component types, so we inline the (trivial) proofs here.
  ≑-refl : {θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ≑ θ
  ≑-refl = (λ z → z) , (λ z → z)

  ≑-sym : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ≑ φ → φ ≑ θ
  ≑-sym = swap

  ≑-trans : {θ φ ψ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ≑ φ → φ ≑ ψ → θ ≑ ψ
  ≑-trans (θ⊆φ , φ⊆θ) (φ⊆ψ , ψ⊆φ) = (λ p → φ⊆ψ (θ⊆φ p)) , (λ p → φ⊆θ (ψ⊆φ p))

  -- The implicit congruence (and level) arguments of the helper lemmas are bound
  -- by lambdas and forwarded explicitly: they cannot be inferred through the
  -- (non-injective) `Con 𝑨 ℓ` carrier type at these function-typed fields.
  ≑-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence (_≑_ {ℓ})
  ≑-isEquivalence {ℓ} = record
    { refl = λ {θ} → ≑-refl {ℓ} {θ}
    ; sym = λ {θ} {φ} → ≑-sym {ℓ} {θ} {φ}
    ; trans = λ {θ} {φ} {ψ} → ≑-trans  {ℓ} {θ} {φ} {ψ}
    }

  ⊆-isPartialOrder : IsPartialOrder (_≑_ {ℓ}) _⊆_
  ⊆-isPartialOrder {ℓ} = record
    { isPreorder = record  { isEquivalence = ≑-isEquivalence {ℓ}
                           ; reflexive = λ {θ} {φ} → ⊆-reflexive {ℓ} {θ} {φ}
                           ; trans = λ {θ} {φ} {ψ} → ⊆-trans {ℓ} {θ} {φ} {ψ}
                           }
    ; antisym = λ {θ} {φ} → ⊆-antisym {ℓ} {θ} {φ}
    }
```

#### The bottom and top of the order

The diagonal congruence `𝟘[ 𝑨 ]` (defined in [Setoid.Congruences.Basic][]) is the
*least* congruence: it is contained in every congruence, because a congruence is
reflexive over `≈` and `𝟘[ 𝑨 ]` relates only `≈`-equal pairs.  The total congruence
`𝟙[ 𝑨 ]` is the *greatest*: every congruence is contained in it, since it relates
everything.  These are the `⊥` and `⊤` of the congruence lattice.

```agda
  -- 𝟘[ 𝑨 ] is the least congruence (the minimum of the containment order).
  𝟘-min : {ℓ : Level}(θ : Con 𝑨 (ρ ⊔ ℓ)) → 𝟘[ 𝑨 ] {ℓ} ⊆ θ
  𝟘-min θ p = reflexive (proj₂ θ) (lower p)

  -- 𝟙[ 𝑨 ] is the greatest congruence (the maximum of the containment order).
  𝟙-max : {ℓ : Level}(θ : Con 𝑨 ℓ) → θ ⊆ 𝟙[ 𝑨 ] {ℓ}
  𝟙-max θ _ = lift tt
```

#### Meet: the intersection of two congruences

The intersection `θ ∩ φ` holds at `(x , y)` exactly when both `θ` and `φ` do.  It
is again a congruence: it contains the setoid equality (reflexivity), it is an
equivalence relation (componentwise), and it is compatible with every basic
operation (componentwise, using the compatibility of `θ` and of `φ`).  We define
the underlying relation first, then bundle the `IsCongruence` proof.

```agda
  -- The underlying relation of the meet: pointwise conjunction.
  meetRel : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → BinaryRel 𝕌[ 𝑨 ] ℓ
  meetRel θ φ x y = proj₁ θ x y × proj₁ φ x y

  _∧_ : Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ → Con 𝑨 ℓ
  θ ∧ φ = meetRel θ φ , mkcon m-reflexive m-isEquivalence m-compatible
    where
    θc = proj₂ θ
    φc = proj₂ φ
    θe = is-equivalence θc
    φe = is-equivalence φc

    open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] using ( _≈_ )
    -- The meet contains the setoid equality because θ and φ both do.
    m-reflexive : ∀ {a₀ a₁} → a₀ ≈ a₁ → meetRel θ φ a₀ a₁
    m-reflexive e = reflexive θc e , reflexive φc e

    open IsEquivalence using (refl ; sym ; trans )
    -- The meet is an equivalence relation, proved componentwise.
    m-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence (meetRel θ φ)
    m-isEquivalence .refl = θe .refl , φe .refl
    m-isEquivalence .sym = λ (p , q) → θe .sym p , φe .sym q
    m-isEquivalence .trans = λ (p , q) (p′ , q′) → θe .trans p p′ , φe .trans q q′

    -- The meet is compatible with every basic operation, componentwise.
    m-compatible : 𝑨 ∣≈ meetRel θ φ
    m-compatible 𝑓 uv = is-compatible θc 𝑓 (λ i → proj₁ (uv i))
                      , is-compatible φc 𝑓 (λ i → proj₂ (uv i))
  infixl 7 _∧_
```

The meet is the *greatest lower bound* of its two arguments: it is below each of
them, and it is above any common lower bound.  These three facts are exactly the
`Infimum` of `_⊆_` at `_∧_`.

```agda
  ∧-lowerˡ : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ∧ φ ⊆ θ
  ∧-lowerˡ = proj₁

  ∧-lowerʳ : {θ φ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → θ ∧ φ ⊆ φ
  ∧-lowerʳ = proj₂

  ∧-greatest : {θ φ ψ : Con 𝑨 ℓ} → ψ ⊆ θ → ψ ⊆ φ → ψ ⊆ θ ∧ φ
  ∧-greatest ψ⊆θ ψ⊆φ p = ψ⊆θ p , ψ⊆φ p

  -- As above, the implicit congruence arguments of ∧-lowerˡ/ʳ and ∧-greatest
  -- are not inferable from the expected component types, so we inline them.
  ∧-infimum : Infimum (_⊆_ {ℓ}) _∧_
  ∧-infimum θ φ = proj₁ , proj₂ , λ ψ ψ⊆θ ψ⊆φ p → ψ⊆θ p , ψ⊆φ p

  open IsMeetSemilattice

  ∧-isMeetSemilattice : IsMeetSemilattice (_≑_ {ℓ}) _⊆_ _∧_
  ∧-isMeetSemilattice .isPartialOrder = ⊆-isPartialOrder
  ∧-isMeetSemilattice .infimum = ∧-infimum
```

#### The poset and meet-semilattice of congruences

Finally we assemble the standard-library bundles.  At a fixed relation level `ℓ`,
`Con-Poset 𝑨` is the poset `(Con 𝑨, ≑, ⊆)` and `Con-MeetSemilattice 𝑨` equips it
with the meet `_∧_`.  (The full lattice and complete lattice, with the join and
the bounds `⊥`/`⊤`, are built in the subsequent steps of #271.)

```agda
module _ (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρ) {ℓ : Level} where
  Con-Poset : Poset (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ)
  Con-Poset = record  { Carrier = Con 𝑨 ℓ ; _≈_ = _≑_ ; _≤_ = _⊆_
                      ; isPartialOrder  = ⊆-isPartialOrder }

  Con-MeetSemilattice : MeetSemilattice (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ)
  Con-MeetSemilattice = record  { Carrier = Con 𝑨 ℓ
                                ; _≈_ = _≑_
                                ; _≤_ = _⊆_
                                ; _∧_ = _∧_
                                ; isMeetSemilattice  = ∧-isMeetSemilattice
                                }
```

#### The bounds: zero and total congruences

The bottom congruence `0ᴬ` is the **diagonal** congruence `𝟘[ 𝑨 ]` and the top
congruence `1ᴬ` is the **total** congruence `𝟙[ 𝑨 ]`, both from
[Setoid.Congruences.Basic][], taken at the absorbing level `L`.  Their minimality
and maximality are the order facts `𝟘-min` / `𝟙-max` of
[Setoid.Congruences.Lattice][].

(The least congruence is the diagonal — the identity relation viewed as a
congruence — not the empty relation: the empty relation is not even reflexive, so
it is not a congruence at all.  An earlier version defined `0ᴬ = Cg 0A` as the
congruence *generated by* the empty relation; that is in fact the diagonal, since
`Cg` closes under reflexivity over `≈`, but the direct definition `𝟘[ 𝑨 ]` is the
standard and clearer one.)

```agda

  1ᴬ : Conᴸ
  1ᴬ = 𝟙[ 𝑨 ] {L}
```

minimum).

#### Infinitary meets and joins

For a family `f : I → Con 𝑨 {L}` indexed by `I : Type ℓ₀`, the infinitary meet is the
intersection `⋀ f` (which holds at `(x , y)` iff every `f i` does), and the
infinitary join is the congruence generated by the union, `⋁ f = Cg(⋃ f)`.  Both stay
at level `L` because `I` is `ℓ₀`-small.  The meet is the greatest lower bound and the
join the least upper bound of the family.

```agda
  module _ {I : Type ℓ₀} (f : I → Conᴸ) where

    -- Infinitary meet: the intersection of the family.
    ⋀ : Conᴸ
    ⋀ = (λ x y → (i : I) → proj₁ (f i) x y) , mkcon m-refl m-equiv m-comp
      where
      open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ] using ( _≈_ )
      m-refl : ∀ {a₀ a₁} → a₀ ≈ a₁ → (i : I) → proj₁ (f i) a₀ a₁
      m-refl e i = reflexive (proj₂ (f i)) e

      m-equiv : IsEquivalence (λ x y → (i : I) → proj₁ (f i) x y)
      m-equiv = record
        { refl   = λ i → IsEquivalence.refl (is-equivalence (proj₂ (f i)))
        ; sym    = λ p i → IsEquivalence.sym (is-equivalence (proj₂ (f i))) (p i)
        ; trans  = λ p q i → IsEquivalence.trans (is-equivalence (proj₂ (f i))) (p i) (q i)
        }

      m-comp : 𝑨 ∣≈ (λ x y → (i : I) → proj₁ (f i) x y)
      m-comp g h i = is-compatible (proj₂ (f i)) g (λ k → h k i)

    -- Infinitary join: the congruence generated by the union of the family.
    ⋁ : Conᴸ
    ⋁ = Cg (λ x y → Σ[ i ∈ I ] proj₁ (f i) x y)

    ⋀-lower : (i : I) → ⋀ ⊆ f i
    ⋀-lower i p = p i

    ⋀-greatest : (ψ : Conᴸ) → (∀ i → ψ ⊆ f i) → ψ ⊆ ⋀
    ⋀-greatest ψ ψ⊆f p i = ψ⊆f i p

    ⋁-upper : (i : I) → f i ⊆ ⋁
    ⋁-upper i p = base (i , p)

    ⋁-least : (ψ : Conᴸ) → (∀ i → f i ⊆ ψ) → ⋁ ⊆ ψ
    ⋁-least ψ f⊆ψ = Cg-least {𝑨 = 𝑨} ψ (λ (i , p) → f⊆ψ i p)
```

Packaging the order with the infinitary operations and their universal properties
yields the complete lattice of congruences.

```agda

    { Carrier          = Conᴸ
    ; _≈_              = _≑_
    ; _≤_              = _⊆_
    ; isPartialOrder   = ⊆-isPartialOrder
    ; ⨆                = ⋁
    ; ⨅                = ⋀

    ; ⨆-least          = λ f x h → ⋁-least f x h
    ; ⨅-lower          = λ f i → ⋀-lower f i
    ; ⨅-greatest       = λ f x h → ⋀-greatest f x h
    }
```
